findings.situation: A filer has a qualified trade or business loss from an earlier year that was held back by another Code provision (for example the passive activity, at-risk or basis rules) and is allowed in figuring 2025 taxable income. That loss was never part of the 2024 Form 8995 line 16 carryforward, so a filer answering the question truthfully leaves it out of line 3.
findings.source_text: i8995 p. 4, Line 3: "Include here the qualified portion of trade or business (loss) carryforward allowed in calculating taxable income in the current year ... See ... Tracking Losses or Deductions Suspended by Other Provisions"; i8995 p. 4, Line 1: "Do not include here ... any portion of qualified losses or deductions previously suspended by other Code provisions that are allowed in calculating taxable income in the current year. For qualified business net (loss) carryforward from the prior year, see instructions for line 3."
findings.why: The instructions send the qualified portion of losses that were held back and are now allowed to line 3, not line 1(c). The question asks only for the 2024 line 16 figure, so it misses those losses and line 3 comes out too small.

locators: p. 1, Who Can Take the Deduction (owner: Form 8995-A with business income refused)

p. 4, Line 3, "Include here the qualified portion of trade or business (loss) carryforward allowed in calculating taxable income in the current year"; p. 5, Line 16, "This is the amount to be carried forward to the next year" (owner: the printed amount)

findings.situation: A filer whose box 5 amount includes REIT shares held 45 days or less, or dividends on positions where they must make related payments, is told only to confirm 'holding-period and related-payment requirements' without being told what those requirements are or what to enter when only part of box 5 qualifies.
findings.source_text: i8995 p. 3: "Qualified REIT dividends include any dividends you received from a REIT held for more than 45 days and for which the payment isn't obligated to someone else"
findings.why: The help never states the more-than-45-day rule or the no-obligation-to-pay rule. An ordinary filer could reasonably read 'once the requirements are met' in two ways: (1) enter the full box 5 amount as a pass/fail test, which could be zero or the full amount, or (2) enter only the qualifying part. Those two readings give different amounts for line 6.

locators: p. 5, Instructions for Recipient, "Box 5. Shows the portion of the amount in box 1a that may be eligible for the 20% qualified business income deduction under section 199A"
